title: On the dogfood, a 4K HDR film that must be re-encoded plays without stalling, on workers running apart on the nodes that can hold it
description: D-038 left the dogfood's 4K HDR re-encode stall a gap; JS-154 measured that one 4-core worker cannot hold the job and that helpers cannot exist with one worker. This task closes the gap on the dogfood or says it stays open: workers as their own pods on the nodes JS-163 measured, sharing one S3 bucket as the transcode store (D-049). It deploys and proves; it builds nothing in jellyscale. D-045.
acceptanceCriteria: Starts only when JS-162's and JS-163's figures have gone to the product owner as a brief (every option priced, keeping the film at real time among them) and the owner has decided the shared transcode store; each homelab change is brought to the owner before it is made. If the figures show more workers cannot bring the film to real time, nothing is deployed and the task returns to the product owner

A worker runs with --roles=worker as its own pod on the 12-thread node; the 4-core node's pod keeps its worker role; no worker runs on the 6-processor node. Each reaches Postgres, every library and the one transcode store, an S3 bucket (transcodeStore: s3://...) in the owner's homelab. The 12-thread node's reserved requests are read first, and the worker's CPU request and limit are recorded with the reason. (D-049)

From jellyfin-web, a 4K HDR re-encode without a subtitle and one with a burned-in image subtitle each play 10 minutes with a seek: speed at or above 1.0 after the first 30 seconds, no segment request over 5 seconds after the start; recorded with ids and counts only. Amended by D-049: no more than 3 freezes of 0.5 seconds or more per 10 minutes, none over 2 seconds; three plays each; also with a subtitle extraction running beside the job. Freezes in the first 30 seconds after each start and each seek are recorded apart from the rest, with their lengths (D-051). Amended by D-065: after the sizing correction the start without a subtitle and one burned-in start were played again, one run each, and met the bound. The second burned-in start, the seek, the three plays each and the play beside a subtitle extraction are closed as not re-measured after the correction, and the record says so.
A play the cluster cannot hold is refused within seconds with its reason, never a stall, once JS-161 is deployed
The time from a worker pod's creation to its first claimed job is measured on each node and recorded for JS-057
A defect found in jellyscale becomes a brief, not a fix here
docs/running.md gains what running workers apart needed; docs/status.md's known gap is closed or says what is still open; no film title, path or host name anywhere

On the S3 bucket, measured between the nodes before the plays: the time from a worker finishing a segment to `stream` on another node serving it, for 100 segments; recorded. No shared store has been measured between machines (JS-162 used one machine's directory). (D-049)

Each worker's declared transcodeCores (from JS-163's figures, brought to the owner as a homelab change) and the speed of each job are recorded; a job slower than real time on a worker whose declared capacity covers it, or slower than expected by more than a fifth, is reported with what ran beside it. (D-049, D-062) Amended by D-064: the declared figures are corrected from this task's own job speeds, and the 12-thread node's worker gets CPU requests equal to limits in whole cores so ffmpeg is not throttled (each a homelab change brought to the owner). Only the parts that missed the bound are played again. A miss in the first 30 seconds after a seek is recorded for JS-174. A burned-in miss that remains returns as a brief. That the cluster holds one 4K play is recorded in docs/status.md, not chased here. Amended by D-065: 'only the parts that missed the bound are played again' is closed at two of four. The declared 3.2 stays until JS-177. No further sizing change is made to the dogfood, except dropping the declared figures when JS-177 merges.
notes: ux: true. The store is an S3 bucket (owner's answer, 2026-11-21: the owner sets up an S3 service in the homelab; the lead chose S3, option 1 of D-049, so workers can run on any node). Each homelab change is still brought to the owner before it is made. Done 2026-11-23 on D-065, with parts not re-measured; nothing unmeasured is written as passing. Figures and method are in docs/transcoding.md ('A 4K HDR re-encode on the dogfood's 12-thread worker'). Per criterion: (1) Taken: started on the owner's decision of the shared S3 store (D-049); each homelab change was brought to the owner first, the D-064 sizing correction included. (2) Taken: the worker runs as its own pod on the 12-thread node, the 4-core node's pod keeps its worker role, no worker on the 6-processor node. CPU limit 8 and request 500m at first; limit 12 and request 6 after D-064's correction, the request below the limit because the node's other workloads request 4.85 of its 12 threads and 7 or 12 would not schedule (a departure from D-064's requests equal to limits). (3) Partly taken. At limit 8: 8 runs, 16 parts (a start and a seek each), three films; 12 parts within 3 freezes of 0.5 s or more after the first 30 s, 4 missed (three starts on one film: 4, 15 and 9 freezes, a burned-in seek on another film, a Dolby Vision profile 7 one: 25 freezes, longest 2.0 s). The first 30 s of every part were recorded apart: none in the starts but two burned-in ones, 0.75 to 2.75 s in each of the 8 seeks (three over 2 s), which is JS-174's. After the correction: the start without a subtitle and one burned-in start of 600 s, one run each, the same specs as two of the misses with their stored segments deleted first, at job speeds of 1.36 and 1.285 (1.032 and 0.995 before), 1.000 after the first 30 s, no freeze of 0.5 s or more anywhere, no segment request over 5 s. NOT taken after the correction: the second burned-in start, the seek, three plays of each part, any play beside a subtitle extraction (none of the runs had one). (4) Taken at limit 8 only: with a 4K play running, 4 PlaybackInfo requests for a second 4K film came back RateLimitExceeded in 12 to 52 ms and jellyfin-web's dialog said 'rate limits' 790 ms after the click; not observed again after the CPU limit went to 12. (5) Taken: pod creation to first claimed job, the 12-thread worker 1.7 and 5.5 s in two restarts (creation times are whole seconds), the 4-core node's pod 7.7 s in one of three restarts, the other two claiming at 37 and 58 s, which was not looked into. (6) Taken: no jellyscale code changed; what was found went to briefs (D-064, D-065, BL-261). (7) Taken for docs/status.md (the gap is narrowed, not closed: the dogfood holds one 4K HDR re-encode at a time) and docs/transcoding.md, the two changes D-065 named; docs/running.md was not changed and was not examined for what running workers apart needed, so that part is NOT taken and comes to triage. (8) NOT taken as written: the criterion asks for 100 segments from a worker finishing one to a stream replica on another node serving it. What was measured, by the measuring session's report (p50 14 ms, max 57 ms), was the time to the response headers of stored segments through a stream replica, from a script that reads at most 40; its output was not kept with the run files. No 100-segment measurement exists; it comes to triage. (9) Taken, with D-065's amendment: the declared figure of the 12-thread worker corrected from 3.5 to 3.2 and its CPU limit raised from 8 to 12; the 4-core worker's 3 unchanged (it cannot hold a 3.2 job); job speeds recorded (at limit 8, 0.897 to 1.137, median 0.97, 11 of 16 below 1.0 on a worker declaring 3.5 for a price of 3.2; what ran beside them was not recorded); 3.2 is conservative, about 3.4 to 3.6 by two runs. Only 2 of the 4 missed parts were played again. Unverified after the fix: the second burned-in start and the burned-in seek were not re-measured, and the last figures for them (0.984 with 9 freezes; 0.963 with 25, longest 2.0 s, first 30 s of the seek 2.5 s) are from before the correction and missed the bound; the two parts that passed passed once each, not three times, and neither ran beside a subtitle extraction; the declared 3.4 to 3.6 is derived from two job speeds and was not run as a declared figure; the request is 6 under a limit of 12 and the node's other workloads request 4.85 of its 12 threads, the speeds hold for whatever those workloads used during the two runs, which was not recorded, and the speed when they use their full requests is unknown; that a second 4K play is still refused within seconds with its reason was observed before the correction and not afterwards; the first replay (1.000 on all four parts, no job rows) served stored segments and is evidence of nothing, so it is never cited; scope is one film for the passed parts, one cluster, one worker with no helper (the 4-core worker declares 3 and cannot help; nothing here says what a shared play does on the dogfood). Criteria 7 (docs/running.md) and 8 were not taken and come back in triage; no run is made for them now (D-065).
